coach.why: Good help should fit the way you want to learn.
coach.body: Choose your coach’s name, style, answer length, focus and creativity. Low creativity keeps t.ROY on the usual path. High creativity adds one less obvious option and says which is which. The middle of the slider changes nothing. Use the Save control to keep those choices. Direct or warm changes the delivery; it does not make a suggestion more accurate. The decision log explains recorded suggestions, not hidden AI reasoning.

accessibility.body: Explore text size, comfortable or compact layout, and motion. Reading help includes plain language, read aloud and the coach’s reply language. Spanish replies do not translate the whole interface. These controls are separate, so you can choose what helps. Verify a change after returning to the page.

privacy.try: Review the actual sharing choices before granting access. Only change one when you understand its scope.

security.why: Your work needs a reliable account you can access.

security.try: Check that you can reach your sign-in email before changing account security.

data.title: Keep a copy. Delete deliberately.

help.try: When ready, take the orientation check. You can review any lesson and retry without losing access.

security.title: Your Data: Who Sees It
security.intro: We built this tool for people who need to trust it. Here's exactly how we protect you.

collect.title: What We Collect
collect.resume: Your resume text, so we can find your skills and match you to jobs
collect.answers: Your answers to Forge questions, so we can match jobs and resources to your situation
collect.refinery: Your activity in the Refinery, so we can track your progress and suggest next steps
collect.chats: Your chats with t.ROY, if you are signed in and turned on Better help, so he can remember your recent work. You can delete them anytime in Settings.
collect.connect: Some basic facts about how you connect: your IP address, your device type, and the rough city it points to. We use them to stop abuse and to show you where you are signed in.
collect.noTrack: We do not track what you do on other sites, and we do not look at your social media.

who.title: Who Can See Your Data
who.banner: You decide. Program staff cannot read your work unless you share it.
who.nothing: <lead>If you share nothing:</lead> your name is not on their caseload list. They cannot read your resume, letters, jobs or anything you wrote. Staff who signed you up, or who you shared with before, may still see your name, email and step.
who.progress: <lead>If you share your progress:</lead> they see your name, email, your step, how many jobs you saved and applied to, when you were last on, and if you got hired. They also see how many times you practiced and whether you made a record plan. They cannot read either one.
who.more: <lead>You can share more, one item at a time,</lead> if your program offers it: your job applications, your resumes or your cover letters. You see what each one shows first. Staff can read them. They cannot change them.
who.noRead: <lead>No program can read these through sharing:</lead> your record plan (what you make in the Disclosure Planner), {checks, select, yes {your saved record checks, } other {}}your interview practice, or your Vault files.
who.stop: <lead>Stop any time in Settings.</lead> That ends new viewing. It cannot take back what someone already read or wrote down.
who.logged: <lead>You can see who looked.</lead> Where your program uses the full workspace, each time staff open something you shared is logged, and you can see the list in Settings.
who.rule: <lead>If a program has its own sharing rule,</lead> you see the rule and its reason first. Nothing opens until you say you saw it, and we will not call it your choice.
who.law: A boss, a PO or the police do not get in just because of who they are. If the law makes us hand something over, we have to.
who.staff: Our own staff can open an account to help you when you ask for support or something breaks. Each time is logged with who and when.

lives.title: Where Your Data Lives
lives.db: Stored in a database that is encrypted at rest. If someone stole the physical disks, they could not read your data.
lives.https: Every connection uses HTTPS, so your data is encrypted while it moves between your device and our servers
lives.vault: Files you upload to your Vault get a second lock on top of the database: each one is sealed with AES-256-GCM encryption tied to your account, so it can only be opened for you.

ai.title: What the AI Sees
ai.job: The AI reads your resume and answers to help you. That's its only job.
ai.record: Most AI steps leave a short record: which tool ran, which AI model, and a short note about the step. The note does not include the words you typed, and the record does not keep a copy of what the AI wrote to you.
ai.memory: When you are signed in and Better help is on, t.ROY remembers your recent chats so he can pick up where you left off. You can delete that history anytime. Without an account, t.ROY does not save your chats.
ai.versions: When you are signed in, each checked version of your resume is saved to your account, with the answers you gave about its lines. You can download or delete them in Settings.
ai.recordStep: The record check is the only screen that asks for your offense, and it asks for your yes first. What you type there goes to Anthropic, which picks items for your checklist from our own list. If you type your record somewhere else, like the chat or the disclosure planner, the AI sees it there too. A saved checklist keeps the list and the state, and keeps what you typed only if you tick the box for it. Taking back your yes deletes your saved checklists.
ai.recordPlain: If you type your record in the chat or the disclosure planner, the AI sees it there.
ai.never: The AI never shares your information with other users

export.title: Export Your Data
export.description: Download a copy of your data: your resume, Forge results, applications, chat history, and more. You can pick which parts to include. We ask you to confirm it's you first.

delete.title: Delete Your Data or Account
delete.description: You choose: delete just your data and keep your login, or delete your whole account. Either way it's a two-step action. You confirm it's you, then confirm again. It can't be undone. Short AI records from before you signed in are not tied to your account, so they stay. They hold no name and none of your words. Abuse-prevention counts are deleted after 30 days.

consent.title: Consent Preferences
consent.description: Manage optional sharing in Settings. You can stop access through the sharing feature; copies and program records already made may remain.

noAccount.title: No Account Required
noAccount.description: The Forge works without an account. We don't save your resume or answers on our servers unless you sign in. Your work stays saved in this web browser until you start over, press Clear this computer, or leave it untouched for a day. On a shared or library computer, press Clear this computer when you finish. To stop abuse we count uses per internet connection, kept as a code made from your IP address that changes every day, never the address itself, and deleted after 30 days. Short AI records say which step ran, not what you typed.

oneAccount.title: One Free Account
oneAccount.description: The Forge asks you to sign in with a free account, the same one the Refinery uses. That is how your work follows you to another device, and how you can download or delete it in Settings. Until it is saved to your account, your work also sits in this web browser. On a shared or library computer, sign out and press Clear this computer when you finish. To stop abuse we count uses per account and per internet connection. The connection is kept as a code made from your IP address that changes every day, never the address itself, and deleted after 30 days. Short AI records say which step ran, not what you typed. The free resume check works without signing in and saves nothing.

lock.title: Locking Down Your Account
lock.password: Set a password, or sign in with a one-time magic link sent to your email. Passwords are stored as a scrambled hash, not as the words you typed.
lock.twoStep: Turn on two-step verification. Every sign-in then asks for a code from an authenticator app, whether you use a password, an email link, or Google, and you get one-time backup codes in case you lose your phone. The secret behind those codes is stored encrypted.
lock.devices: See every device signed in to your account and sign out any one you don't recognize. It loses access right away.
lock.proof: Exporting or deleting your data asks you to prove it's you first, with your password, or by typing DELETE if you use magic-link sign-in. That way a borrowed or unlocked device can't wipe or copy your data.

choice.title: What You Share Is Your Choice
choice.intro: You control a few separate choices in Settings. You can change any of them anytime:
choice.better: Better help: let the AI use more of your Forge answers to give you sharper, more personal suggestions.
choice.research: Research: allow your data, with your name and details removed, to help study what helps people find work.
choice.outcomes: Outcomes: share whether you landed a job so partner programs can see if this is working. You can share this without sharing anything else.

dont.title: What We Don't Do
dont.networks: No ad networks and no data brokers. We count visits with Google Analytics and Vercel to see which tools help people. They see which pages get used, not what you type. We keep them off disclosure practice, interview practice, the Vault, your documents, and invitation links that carry a code or a name.
dont.providers: We use service providers for hosting, storage, AI, email, bot checks, job listings and visit counting. Program sharing and legally required disclosures are described above.
dont.surprises: No surprises. If something changes, we'll tell you first

orgs.title: For Organizations
orgs.intro: If you're considering this platform for your clients:
orgs.staff: Staff access to participant materials is limited by organization, staff permissions and the participant's active sharing grants
orgs.record: Most AI steps leave a short record (tool, model, time) for review. The record does not hold the AI's full reply.
orgs.voice: Voice practice audio passes through OpenAI, which may retain it up to 30 days for abuse monitoring. We do not store the audio. If the person chooses to save a practice run, we keep the written words, encrypted.
orgs.users: Users control their own data. They can export or delete it on their own, without going through you
orgs.rate: Rate limiting protects against abuse. Programs that share one internet connection can use an access code so their group gets a bigger shared limit.
orgs.codes: Partner access codes let you onboard your clients with elevated permissions
